findings.quote_bytes: (3) RANGE (close_t - low_t)/(high_t - low_t) >= 0.5  ...  CLV_t = ((C-L)-(H-C))/(H-L) per FOREX-NG7 §5 FNG7-A2-P1-ABSORB
findings.why_wrong: Both formulas have a zero denominator when high_t == low_t (zero-range session). On the death-inclusive cohort with stale low-volume names such sessions exist, and the CLV-RANGE family carries no participation filter, so bookable names with zero-range prints enter P_t/slope. The degenerate-case convention (exclude the session, treat CLV as 0/1, carry last value, ...) is unpinned at plan level and is not explicitly named in the D1 manifest required-fields list ('per-configuration full construction definitions' arguably covers it but nothing forces the convention to be visible). Different conventions produce different fired sets and state series, which can move W_c and selection order in knife-edge cases.
findings.required_remediation: One-sentence pin before D1: the manifest must declare, per affected configuration, the zero-range session convention (recommended: exclude the session from RANGE/CLV computation and census the excluded count), and the count of degenerate sessions must be reported at D2.

findings.quote_bytes: rolling-beta state; DGS10-LEVEL state; event-calendar geometry (P-24 class); ...  Disposition rule: a control that is unpopulated or has an invalid null is NOT_ADJUDICABLE, never silently skipped.
findings.why_wrong: DGS10-LEVEL is enumerated in the R0 shadow inventory, but STOCKS-NG6 (same /eod-only data plane, same estate) recorded 'DGS10 UNMEASURABLE' at its D2 — a known lineage fact the plan imports without the tag or a disposition. The §6 disposition rule covers CONTROLS ('unpopulated or invalid null'), not shadows; 'under-enumerated inventory = invalid PASS' covers enumeration, not measurement failure. The disposition of an enumerated-but-unmeasurable shadow is therefore unpinned, with a split precedent (NG6: record UNMEASURABLE, disclose, proceed with measured shadows; STOCKS-NG2: unmeasurable decisive veto shadow => configuration fail-closed INELIGIBLE). The fork ranges from invalid-PASS risk (silent skip) to a whole-cycle 0/3 close — a conclusion-level fork left to implementer choice.
findings.required_remediation: Pin the rule before D2, e.g.: a shadow recorded UNMEASURABLE is printed as UNMEASURABLE with cause on every D2 artifact; W_c is computed over the measurable set and every affected configuration is labelled PARTIALLY_ADJUDICATED_R0 in the D2 output and the S freeze (or, if the stricter NG2 reading is intended, say so). Either pin is valid; silence is not.

findings.quote_bytes: Family tier value T_F = min over the family's D2-surviving configurations of W_c (the family's best-case distance from lethal ancestry)
findings.why_wrong: The parenthetical gloss is imprecise: W_c = max |pooled_rho| is ancestry EXPOSURE (larger = closer to lethal ancestry), so T_F = min of that is the family's best-case ancestry exposure, not a 'distance' (a true distance would rank descending). The operative rule ('families ASCENDING by T_F — most novel first' + stated rationale) is unambiguous and mechanical, so no behavior fork; only the gloss could mislead.
findings.required_remediation: Replace the gloss with 'best-case (minimum over surviving configurations) ancestry exposure; lower = more novel' or delete it.

findings.quote_bytes: selection is FAMILY-STRATIFIED round-robin over the tier-ordered families — one configuration per family per round, at most 2 scored cells per family, until 3 cells are filled
findings.why_wrong: T_F is defined over 'D2-surviving configurations'; a family with zero D2 survivors has undefined T_F and undefined round-robin behavior. Mechanically it contributes no cells, but the skip semantics (family removed from the tier order before ranking; disclosed) are unstated.
findings.required_remediation: Pin: families with zero D2-surviving configurations are removed from the tier order before ranking, with the removal and cause disclosed in the D2/S artifacts.

findings.quote_bytes: minimum twin population 10 fired decisions per bucket per fold — a sub-floor bucket is NOT_ADJUDICABLE and disclosed, never silently skipped; must NOT out-earn the candidate (the R6 clock rule extends to it)
findings.why_wrong: When one or more buckets are sub-floor NOT_ADJUDICABLE, the plan does not state how the control-level 'must NOT out-earn' comparison aggregates the remaining populated buckets (per-bucket majority, pooled expectancy, equal-weight). The C-CAL-HIST matching rule is a required fail-closed D1-manifest field, which mitigates determinism risk, but the control-level verdict semantics under partial sub-floor should be pinned at plan level so the manifest rule cannot quietly choose a survivor-favorable aggregation.
findings.required_remediation: Pin: the control-level comparison aggregates populated buckets by the manifest-declared rule, and if any fired bucket of the candidate is sub-floor the affected bucket's candidate leg is disclosed and excluded symmetrically (or the whole control is NOT_ADJUDICABLE fail-closed) — one of the two, frozen.
